currentMechanics.capitalSizing: allocateAndBuildPlans uses post-consensus priorityScore proportionally, subject to deployment ratio and 35% cap

structuralFindings: Consensus can change the first comparator directly through the additive bonus.
The same post-consensus priorityScore also affects planned capital sizing.
marketConsensusScore is a separate third comparator only when post-consensus priorityScore and raw RR tie.
The base PriorityScore components already sum to 100 maximum before consensus; the external bonus can therefore increase score saturation/compression near 100.
A +7 consensus bonus is equivalent in absolute PriorityScore points to 25 setupQuality points at the 28% setup weight, or 50 points of any 14%-weighted base component.
SourceCount>=5 saturates the additive bonus at +7 while consensusScore can still rise from 95 to 100 at sourceCount 6; this distinction matters only in tie situations for the third comparator.
